title: Fall from Height
disclaimer: REAL MEDICATION INFORMATION — FIVEM ROLE-PLAY ONLY. This content is fictionalised for FiveM gameplay and must not be used to diagnose or treat a real person. In a real emergency, call 999 or 112.
incident_description: A patient who has fallen from a height such as a roof, balcony, ladder, scaffolding, building, staircase, tree or cliff. Injury severity depends on height, landing surface, body position, body region impacted and whether the patient struck another object during the fall.
scene_safety: Confirm the scene is safe before approaching.
Check for unstable structures, falling objects, electricity, fire, water, traffic, broken glass and unsafe ground.
Do not enter an unstable building or structure.
Request police, fire and additional medical resources where appropriate.
Identify the height of the fall and the landing surface.
Determine whether the patient landed on their head, neck, back, chest, abdomen, pelvis or limbs.
Establish whether the patient was trapped, impaled or crushed.
Consider whether the fall may have been related to assault, intoxication, medical collapse or self-harm.
Preserve evidence and follow safeguarding or police procedures where relevant.
mechanism_questions: Approximately how high was the fall?
Did the patient land head-first, feet-first, on their side or on their back?
Did the patient strike another object before landing?
Was there a loss of consciousness?
Was the patient able to walk after the fall?
Was there a seizure or medical event before the fall?
Was alcohol or drug use suspected?
Was the patient trapped or difficult to access?
Was the patient taking anticoagulants or antiplatelet medicines?
What time did the fall occur?
What treatment has already been given?
initial_impression: Treat a fall from significant height as potentially serious even if the patient is awake and talking.
Observe the patient's position, movement, speech, breathing effort, skin colour and distress.
Look for catastrophic haemorrhage before performing a detailed examination.
Assume spinal injury is possible when the mechanism is high energy, the patient has neck or back pain, neurological symptoms, reduced consciousness or distracting injuries.
Consider head, chest, abdominal, pelvic and limb injuries simultaneously.
Do not allow the patient to stand or walk if spinal, pelvic or lower-limb injury is suspected.

look_for: Bleeding from the chest, abdomen, pelvis or limbs
actions: Apply firm direct pressure to external bleeding.
Use a tourniquet in the RP system for life-threatening limb bleeding not controlled by direct pressure.
Record the time of tourniquet application.
Do not remove soaked dressings to inspect an actively bleeding wound.
Escalate immediately for uncontrolled bleeding or signs of shock.

look_for: Blood or vomit in the mouth
Swelling around the mouth or neck
actions: Ask an alert patient to speak.
Maintain manual in-line spinal protection if spinal injury is suspected.
Use basic airway manoeuvres and suction according to the server's authorised procedures.
Escalate immediately for a threatened or obstructed airway.
Do not give oral medication or fluids to a patient with reduced consciousness or a threatened airway.
Expose the chest enough to assess movement and wounds while preventing heat loss.
Apply an occlusive dressing to an open chest wound according to the server's equipment system.
Escalate urgently for severe respiratory distress, worsening oxygen saturation or suspected tension-pneumothorax-type presentation.
Do not delay transport for a prolonged examination.
Control external haemorrhage.
Establish intravenous access in the RP system if authorised.
Keep the patient warm.
Do not repeatedly rock, compress or test the pelvis.
Apply a pelvic binder in the RP system only when high-energy trauma and suspected pelvic bleeding are present.
Escalate for shock, ongoing bleeding or deteriorating observations.
Record GCS using eye, verbal and motor components.
Repeat neurological observations if there is head injury or abnormal consciousness.
Treat a falling GCS as a time-critical deterioration.
Do not assume intoxication explains abnormal consciousness until serious injury has been considered.
Escalate for GCS below 15, seizure, new neurological deficit or deterioration.
Expose only as much as required to assess injury.
Preserve dignity.
Prevent hypothermia.
Inspect the back only when safe and with sufficient assistance.
Record all visible injuries before covering the patient.

stable_pattern.skin: Warm, normal colour, capillary refill less than 2 seconds

concerning_pattern.skin: Pale, cool or sweaty; capillary refill may be delayed

critical_pattern.heart_rate: 120 bpm or higher, or abnormally slow in a deteriorating patient
critical_pattern.gcs: 8 or less, or a clear downward trend
critical_pattern.skin: Mottled, grey, blue, cold or clammy

observation_rules: Normal initial observations do not exclude serious injury.
Repeat observations after every major intervention and whenever symptoms change.
Record the trend rather than only the latest values.
Interpret observations alongside the mechanism and examination findings.

head_and_face: Blood from the nose or ears
neck_and_spine: New bladder or bowel symptoms where relevant

differential_diagnoses: Drug or alcohol intoxication complicating trauma

critical: Spinal cord injury with neurological deficit

immediate_management: Maintain spinal protection when clinically indicated.
Treat life-threatening problems before minor injuries.
Immobilise suspected fractures in the position found unless an authorised server protocol permits otherwise.
Do not repeatedly manipulate suspected spinal, pelvic or limb injuries.
Minimise time at scene after immediate life-saving interventions.
Pre-alert the receiving hospital for serious or critical trauma.
Transport major trauma to the server's designated major trauma centre.

medications.when_to_consider: Severe traumatic pain after the primary survey, if there is no contraindication.
Major trauma with active or suspected significant haemorrhage within the appropriate time window.

after_initial_assessment: Repeat heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation and GCS.
Repeat pupil assessment if head injury is suspected.
Repeat distal circulation, sensation and movement for limb injuries.
after_medication: Repeat observations within the server's configured interval.
Do not administer further opioid if respiratory rate falls, consciousness deteriorates or oxygen saturation falls.
during_transport: Repeat immediately if the patient deteriorates.
Update the receiving hospital if the condition changes.

escalation_criteria: Fall from significant height with suspected major trauma
Severe chest pain or respiratory distress
Anticoagulant or antiplatelet use with head injury

minor: Only consider minor disposition if the mechanism is low risk, the patient has a reassuring examination, observations are normal and there are no red flags.
Provide RP safety-netting and document the decision.
moderate: Transport to the designated emergency department for clinical assessment and imaging.
serious_or_critical: Pre-alert the designated major trauma centre.
Provide immediate life-saving treatment at scene.
Request senior clinician or specialist backup.
Do not delay transport for a prolonged secondary survey.

handover.template: This is a [age]-year-old [sex] who fell approximately [height] from [object/location] onto [surface] at [time]. The patient landed [body position]. Suspected injuries are [injuries]. Initial observations were HR [value], RR [value], BP [value], SpO2 [value], GCS [value] and pain [value]/10. Key positive findings are [findings]. Key negative findings are [findings]. Treatment given was [treatment and medication]. The response was [response]. Estimated arrival is [time]. Additional requirements are [requirements].
handover.example: This is a 41-year-old following a fall of approximately 5 metres from scaffolding onto concrete at 15:10. The patient landed on their left side and did not lose consciousness. Suspected injuries are left chest trauma, pelvic injury and a left femur fracture. Initial observations are pulse 124, respiratory rate 28, blood pressure 94/60, oxygen saturation 94% on air, GCS 15 and pain 9/10. The patient is pale and clammy with left thigh deformity and abdominal tenderness. External bleeding is controlled. Morphine was administered under the RP medication protocol. The patient remains borderline and is being transferred to the major trauma centre.

documentation: Possible medical event before the fall
Medication name, dose, route, time and response
complications: Missed injury caused by intoxication or altered mental state

example_cases.description: A patient falls from the bottom two steps of a staircase and lands on their hand. They remain alert and have isolated wrist pain.
A patient falls approximately 3 metres from a ladder onto their feet and develops severe ankle pain with deformity. They remain alert and haemodynamically stable.
A patient falls approximately 6 metres from a roof onto concrete. They are confused, pale and tachycardic, with chest pain and abdominal tenderness.
example_cases.likely_diagnosis: Major trauma with suspected internal haemorrhage, chest injury and head injury
